chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day," let him not sleep except with a witr (odd-numbered prayer).

key_terms.وَتْرٍ: Odd-numbered prayer, typically performed at night
key_terms.يَبِيتَنَّ: To spend the night or sleep

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the witr prayer before sleeping in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) establishes the Witr prayer as a nightly seal for the believer, explicitly connecting the ritual to the foundational pillars of faith in Allah and the Last Day. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining spiritual vigilance and continuity of worship until sleep, reflecting the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt in preserving Sunnah practices that reinforce daily devotion.
